papers.title: Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography-Angiography and Longitudinal Changes in Cognition and Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.reason: The study evaluates retinal imaging as a longitudinal biomarker of general cognitive and cerebrovascular change but is not specifically focused on executive function or task-based assessment.

papers.title: Adiposity and Cognitive Performance in Older Men and Women from the Study of Muscle, Mobility and Aging (SOMMA).
papers.reason: The paper concerns correlates of cognitive performance in older adults, but the title provides no indication of executive-function-specific findings or computational modelling.

papers.title: Feasibility of remote self-administered cognitive assessment in an Alzheimer's disease treatment clinic
papers.reason: Remote cognitive assessment is relevant to clinical monitoring, but this feasibility study is not evidently focused on executive-function modelling or multimodal biomarkers.

papers.title: Reactive Compensation for Proactive Deficits in Parkinsons Disease
papers.reason: The paper directly examines the balance between proactive and reactive cognitive control in Parkinson's disease, a central executive-function mechanism that can inform process models.

papers.title: Associations between MoCA screening-positive cognitive impairment, anxiety, depression, and quality of life in patients with oral cancer: a cross-sectional study in China
papers.reason: The study uses a broad cognitive screener in a clinical population but primarily examines associations with mood and quality of life rather than executive function.

papers.title: Evaluation of Autonomic and Cognitive Functions in Patients with Essential Tremor.
papers.reason: The case-control study identifies reduced MoCA performance, particularly in the visuospatial/executive domain, in essential tremor, although cognition is assessed only with a broad screening instrument.

papers.title: Effects of Sleeve Gastrectomy on Cognitive Function, Metabolic Indexes and Related Hormones in Adolescents with Obesity.
papers.reason: The paper evaluates general cognitive changes after a metabolic intervention but is not evidently centred on executive-function mechanisms, modelling, or digital assessment.

papers.title: Potential Contribution of the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis to Doxorubicin-Associated Cognitive Impairment: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.reason: This review covers biological mechanisms that may produce attention and executive deficits after chemotherapy, but its core focus is the microbiota-gut-brain pathway and the evidence is predominantly preclinical.
